page.layout: One printed page of running text in a single column, with marginal notes in the right margin (three at the head of the column, two faint ones lower down). Below the second rule are a few lines of small type, partly legible. Faint mirrored text from the reverse side shows through the middle and lower part of the page and is not transcribed.

main_text.p: Quintus est In eum locum.Theophylactus: GRATIAM autem, non MERCEDEM, dixit à Deo futurum; perinde ac si dicat, Non enim laborum accipitis mercedem, sed per gratiam haec fiunt omnia, in Christo Iesu, qui haec operatur & factitas[?].

Sextus, qui agmen claudit, De Præd. lib. 2. ad Monimum[?].Fulgentius: Cur verò mors STIPENDIUM, vita aeterna GRATIA DEI dicitur: nisi quia illa REDDITUR, haec DONATUR? Sic hi antiqui Patres; nec iis ex tota Antiquitate, quod sciam, Pater ullus adversatur, nè unus quidem. Qui si causam Protestantium consulto dissendere voluissent, non potuissent clarius aut distinctius sensum nostrum exprimere. cit. 1. de [illegible, ~10 letters] 5 Atque haec, &c.
Illustrissimus pro Ecclesia Romana, Co[illegible, ~45 letters]

page.notes: The first two paragraphs are clear, apart from the doubtful readings marked [?]. The bold line below the second rule is partly legible; its remaining lines are too faint to read and are not transcribed. The bottom-right marginal notes are only partly readable. The heavy black mark "CAP." near the lower rule is ink or a stamp and is left out. The faint text in the middle of the page is show-through from the reverse side. The running head is taken from the printed head, which includes "Sect. 3."; the page number 111 is printed at the top right.
